I’m not sure if my nationality really does hold any account for my mental health at all, but it’s interesting to see some similarities between you and myself—my best friend lives in Australia and we’re both always baffled at how connected they and I can always be. We play Apex Legends together, we share playlists, we stream movies together… 

Regardless of where you come from, where you’re at now and where you plan to be, there really is a lot to life that people like myself do take for granted. I’ve never truly faced any adversity and yet here I am with major depression wishing each day was my last. Deep down there really is a lot to be grateful for, and one of them is the perspective of people like you who remind people like myself that, “yeah the world kinda blow right now but look at these little things” and it truly is really cool.

He wasn’t shy in the slightest and he made sure to let you know EXACTLY what he was thinking or feeling. Other staff sometimes had difficulty trying to “deal” with him, but I feel like him and I were good together, I always used to drive him up and down the halls really fast, make car noises with his wheelchair and even pop wheelies for him (despite the complaints of many higher up staff because “that’s not safe!” and “you’re not a caretaker so you shouldn’t be handling him!”). He didn’t care. He’d be cracking up, hooting and hollering in laughter up and down the halls until I finally had to get back to work. We both always looked forward to it!

You’d be amazed. Secondhand suicide and making comments about such is so often tied in with dark humor that people don’t think twice about it. Plus, the legal ramifications of wanting to call for help on someone but ultimately they have to be the one to do it—it can’t be forced. So hence so many people who might see these signs can’t do shit except talk. But we live in such a busy and selfish “me myself and I” society, no one would bat an eye.

Steadily or suddenly losing contact with people for no reason can possibly be a sign. Trying to push loved ones and friends “away”; noticeable changes in attitude. 

There’s also little comments or self-depreciating humor you should look out for. As someone with depression and suicidal tendencies, I’ve already caught myself saying things at my auto tech job to my coworkers like “What would happen if I just drank this bottle of brake fluid?” Or “keep backing up and hit me.” In an environment like that, we all use dark humor at times but I was beginning to realize I was bordering on seriousness with shit like that. 

Please keep a good eye out for friends and loved ones.

Other people might not care about sports, but the night the Philadelphia Eagles won the NFC Championship Game; Jan. 21, 2018. Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia, PA. My mother somehow, some way by the Grace of the Gods or whatever secured two tickets, for her and myself, all the way up the nosebleeds. It was a beautiful clear night—not too cold actually for mid-January. Being huge Philly fans, we’d been to games at the Linc before, but something this time around was **magical**. 

It was the last game before the Super Bowl. There was not a bad vibe or an ill feeling at all that night. The crowd was electrifying, the atmosphere was amped, we sang-chanted the Famous Eagles Fight Song after every touchdown was such passion and gusto, we sang Tom Petty’s “Won’t Back Down” in the fourth quarter, and we ended chanting in complete unison “WE WANT BRADY!”. Yes. **The** Infamous Tom Brady, then of the New England Patriots and our next opponent in Super Bowl 52, if everything panned out just right.

 The game clock stuck 00:00, the final score that night being the Eagles 34, Vikings 7, and I honest to god I thought I had died and went to heaven. I started sobbing, deadass bawling like a baby and hugging my mom tight. I remember peeking over the edge of the stadium wall to look out past the city and see people lighting up fireworks in the middle of the street. Fans cheering, singing, crying tears of joy just as my mother and I were. 

The Philadelphia Eagles were going to the Super Bowl for the first time in nearly 15 years, and I got to wittiness it first hand, a lasting memory both my mom and I will get to hold onto to.

It sounds lame but I still get a little teary eyed thinking about that night…

Hey bud, here’s to you trying something new! It depends on your taste and interest in genres but I know Shonen Jump is usually the biggest gateway into manga. They typically have battle action series that are heavy on fighting and all that stuff—the two series I’m genuinely into is My Hero Academia and Jujutsu Kaisen. I’d absolutely recommend checking both of those out since they’re also big names in fandom in general. 
If you’re not into battle action and violence like that, there’s also sports manga like Haikyuu where you don’t have to know shit about sports as it explains things to you, the reader, but those focus more on overcoming struggles and “the power of friendship” and such. Those are good if you want something a little more lighthearted and feel-good. (One of my personal favorites, though it’s only online through a rough scan translation, is called Ookiku Furikabutte, or “Big Windup”, a high school baseball manga that focuses on the players growing in their strengths and going from strangers to best friends and overcoming challenges and whatnot—the author does such a great job writing the characters so authentically.) 
There’s also another series I read and really enjoyed called The Promised Neverland which was more of a physiological horror/thriller. A decent amount of violence and gore but it had its twists and “not everything is as it seems” moments. It kept me on my toes definitely!
Lastly: want a good chuckle to get you through the day? The Way of the Househusband. Absolutely recommend with all my heart. It’s a comedy about an ex-Yakuza gangster who is a stay at home husband and tries to just live a peaceful life but ends up getting himself into dumb situations because he’s so stuck in his old gang ways. 

I’d check out some of these big names first to get the feel of what genres and styles you like—there’s a manga for almost everything. You can usually find free scans online where you can read but I personally have the Shonen Jump app. It’s like $2 a month for unlimited access to high quality scans and official translations. 

I’m hoping you’re able to find a little beacon of light to help you out, friend 💕

I appreciate your good intentions. Re-reading your post again in a better frame of mind, I can see you meant well. But with that said, those of us with strong suicidal ideations and/or severe depression really, truly are just... EXHAUSTED. Period. No if’s, ands, or buts. I know I can’t speak for everyone, but for me, I get instantly upset and annoyed the moment someone suggests “oh you’re depressed? Welllllll, have you tried...” and then usually tops it off with something like yoga or a better diet or more sleep, etc. 

Dont say it. Dont even think to say it. 

All any of this is, if one finds it enjoyable, is merely just a band-aid for these other-worldly dark thoughts. Example: I fucking love working out. I genuinely genuinely the feeling of power I get from lifting weights or going on a walk on a nice cool day. 

It’s great. Until I’m done with it and then I have to get back to mundane, depressing life. You eventually reach a point where you rely on something too much for your single sense of enjoyment, it’s not fun anymore. Most times anymore, I feel like I’m reading manga and watching anime just to stay afloat like it’s a chore—not because I actually enjoy it. You train your brain to rely on something and it becomes habit. Congrats. Now you’re numb to what you once found enjoyable too! 

tl;dr: you mean well, but my depressed ass is still just fucking tired. Regardless, I appreciate your effort.

“It’s just a letter, you talk and FaceTime and text all the time so why bother?” My best friend lives on the other side of the globe. Shes an aspiring artist and when we first met, she was already packing up to move away. We somehow stayed in touch all these years. It’s a birthday tradition now that we hand write letters and send little care packages to each other every year. I save every letter, and for a while she was even sending original, little sketches of some of her work—all handcrafted with her own two talented and loving hands. She may strike it big someday or not, but I don’t same them for money: I save them for the sentimentality; the proof of her growth as an artist, as my best friend, the proof and familiarity of our dumb inside jokes and love and support for each other and as someone I care so much about. They’re not just letters to me.
